text:
anya: Quick sanity check — AWQ/INT8 bake on a customer H100 box is flaking. CUDA 12.2 image + TRT-LLM plugin. Failing during init, not during inference. Anyone seen this stack?

mike: Which error? driver version mismatch is common when plugin was built with a different CUDA.

sophia: Paste of the failing bits: 
```
2026-02-19T14:12:03Z ERROR trtllm: failed to create engine: /usr/local/lib/libcublasLt.so.12: undefined symbol: cublasLtMM_alphabeta
terminate called after throwing an instance of 'trt::plugin::PluginException'
  what():  trt plugin: symbol lookup error
```

anya: That libcublasLt symbol is the weird part — H100 box has driver 535.x but customer image is CUDA 12.2. Plugin was installed from wheel trt-llm-0.9.2 built against CUDA 13.

raj: Yup — plugin ABI mismatches can manifest like that. vLLM and Triton can also mask it by falling back to CPU if kernels aren't found. Did you see a CPU fallback and huge latency spike?

anya: Exactly. FP8 path tries to bind to trt kernels, fails symbol lookup, then vLLM falls back to a CPU slowpath. End-to-end latency went from ~40ms/token to ~800ms/token. Ouch.

mike: Workarounds we used before:
- rebuild trt-llm against the target CUDA (preferred)
- pin driver+container to matching combo (customer doesn't want driver update)
- use the Triton backend instead of the trt-llm plugin if instrumented; Triton can be more tolerant but still needs lib compatibility

sophia: For testing I made a small reproducer (docker run) — maybe try on the repro box: 
```bash
# reproducer (runs a minimal trt-llm engine init)
docker run --gpus=all --rm -it \
  --entrypoint /bin/bash \
  --env CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 \
  -v $(pwd)/model:/model our-registry/trt-llm:0.9.2-cuda12.2 \
  -c "python -c 'from trtllm import Engine; Engine.load(\"/model/engine.plan\")'"
```

raj: If you can't rebuild plugin, there's a temporary env var we used during a support case: `TRTLLM_DISABLE_SYMBOL_CHECK=1`. It forces a looser symbol resolution and lets the plugin try to JIT fallback kernels, but it is unsafe — only for smoke tests. :warning:

anya: We tried that: it let initialization proceed but then hit subtle numerics causing incorrect logits for FP8 tests. Not safe for customer.

mike: Another angle — convert AWQ->GPTQ fallback weights for this customer path. GPTQ runtime on that stack uses core CUDA kernels (cublas) that exist in CUDA12 layout, so it doesn't rely on trt-llm plugin symbols. We saw ~+5% latency vs trt-llm FP8 but accuracy delta was tiny.

anya: Do we have measured accuracy deltas for AWQ vs GPTQ on this Mistral-like model?

sophia: Quick numbers from our 1k QA prompts:
- FP16 baseline (reference): EM 78.4
- AWQ INT8: EM 77.6 (delta -0.8)
- GPTQ 8-bit: EM 78.1 (delta -0.3)
Throughput: AWQ/FP8 ~1.6x of GPTQ-8 on our H100 cluster when trt-llm works; but when plugin fails, AWQ drops to ~0.15x because of CPU fallback.

raj: So practical guidance: if customer cannot change drivers/plugins, prefer GPTQ path for stability. If they can standardize on a specific CUDA/plugin combo, trt-llm+AWQ gives best unit cost.

anya: Action items:
- sophia: add the repro docker snippet and the libcublasLt error to the infra bug file.
- mike: test building trt-llm wheel against CUDA12.2 and share artifact.
- raj: prepare a customer-facing playbook: "If you see cublasLt symbol errors => options: rebuild plugin / pin container+driver / convert to GPTQ runtime"

infra-bot: deploy-bot: Created issue INFRA-2145 linking logs and repro. Assigned to sophia and mike.

mike: One more note — Triton 23.x + TensorRT 9.6 builds we've used had fewer symbol surprises because the wheels bundle more compat shims. Recommend trying Triton 23.05 image as a middle ground.

anya: Great. I'll loop in the SE handling the customer and propose a stable short-term switch to GPTQ while we validate rebuilt plugin. :thumbsup:

sophia: I'll drop the mini reproducer and a short perf matrix into INFRA-2145. Also will include a small script to convert AWQ->gptq as a fallback: 
```bash
python convert_awq_to_gptq.py --input model.awq.safetensors --output model.gptq.safetensors --calib 256
```

anya: Thanks all — keeping this thread for updates.
